data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for radio frequency management.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for radio frequency management

policy_statements.source_text: This DR supersedes DR 3300-001-C, Radio Frequency Management, dated July 10, 2019.
cross_references: DR 3300-001-C, Radio Frequency Management, dated July 10, 2019

policy_statements.source_text: This DR will be in effect until superseded or the expiration date.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may supplement this DR when developing their internal guidance.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when developing their internal guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR are not allowed.
policy_statements.target: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR

policy_statements.source_text: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR, one copy of each supplement will be forwarded to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Telecommunications Infrastructure Management and Governance (TIMG) at ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov.
conditions: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR

policy_statements.source_text: Per 7 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Section 2.60(a)(27), the Chief of the Forest Service (FS) has been delegated authority by the Under Secretary for Natural Resources and Environment to administer the radio frequency licensing work of the Department.
policy_statements.target: radio frequency licensing work of the Department

policy_statements.source_text: The FS Chief has delegated staff from the FS-Chief Information Office to serve on the following committees:
Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee (IRAC);
policy_statements.actor_name: staff from the FS-Chief Information Office

policy_statements.source_text: Frequency Assignment Subcommittee (FAS);
policy_statements.actor_name: staff from the FS-Chief Information Office

policy_statements.source_text: Technical Subcommittee (TSC); and
policy_statements.actor_name: staff from the FS-Chief Information Office

policy_statements.source_text: Spectrum Planning Subcommittee (SPS) of the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA).
policy_statements.actor_name: staff from the FS-Chief Information Office
policy_statements.target: Spectrum Planning Subcommittee (SPS) of the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to those USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices using radio communications and spectrum management.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices using radio communications and spectrum management

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will contact FS-Frequency Management to obtain spectrum management support and frequency ranges for radio equipment.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA wireless systems will be designed to use current technology, be spectrum efficient, and share resources among Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices whenever it is cost effective and when savings can be achieved.
conditions: whenever it is cost effective and when savings can be achieved

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will adhere to Federal regulations and procedures for spectrum management when establishing and operating wireless communications systems and services.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: Federal regulations and procedures for spectrum management
conditions: when establishing and operating wireless communications systems and services

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices with missions that require a land mobile radio program will develop a strategic plan that describes their Frequency Modulated Land Mobile Radio (FM LMR) use.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: strategic plan that describes their Frequency Modulated Land Mobile Radio (FM LMR) use
conditions: with missions that require a land mobile radio program

policy_statements.source_text: The plan will be reviewed, updated, and submitted annually to the ENS Director.
conditions: annually

policy_statements.source_text: Any device which radiates electromagnetic energy through free space must be authorized prior to procurement or used by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices.
policy_statements.target: Any device which radiates electromagnetic energy through free space
conditions: prior to procurement or used by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Frequency authorization must be obtained before funds can be obligated for the procurement of communications equipment requiring radio frequency authorization for use.
conditions: before funds can be obligated for the procurement of communications equipment requiring radio frequency authorization for use

policy_statements.source_text: Operations on an assigned frequency must be within the parameters of the frequency assignment.

Cellular telephones and other leased personal communications services (PCS) are exempt from this requirement as they are licensed through the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to the service provider.
policy_statements.target: Cellular telephones and other leased personal communications services (PCS)

policy_statements.source_text: Applications or modifications for frequency assignment will be submitted to the USDA FAS Representative.
policy_statements.target: Applications or modifications for frequency assignment

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will contact the USDA FAS Representative for training and software requirements.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Frequency requirements for new systems or major system upgrades must be planned in advance.
policy_statements.target: Frequency requirements for new systems or major system upgrades

policy_statements.source_text: Requests for frequency assignments will be forwarded to the USDA FAS Representative at least 1 year in advance of any planned procurements.
conditions: at least 1 year in advance of any planned procurements

policy_statements.source_text: NTIA has final approval for the frequency assignment requests.
A separate formal frequency assignment request is required for each frequency to be installed in a base station, repeater, group of mobile radios, or group of portable radios in a system.
policy_statements.target: each frequency to be installed in a base station, repeater, group of mobile radios, or group of portable radios in a system

policy_statements.source_text: Sharing of existing USDA systems among Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices will be considered prior to developing a new system or expanding an existing system.
policy_statements.target: Sharing of existing USDA systems among Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices
conditions: prior to developing a new system or expanding an existing system

policy_statements.source_text: Such sharing may be required when spectrum availability is limited, unavailable, or the traffic does not justify a separate system.
conditions: when spectrum availability is limited, unavailable, or the traffic does not justify a separate system

policy_statements.source_text: NTIA’s Manual of Regulations and Procedures for Federal Radio Frequency Management ("Redbook") mandates that Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices consider the use of commercial services in any system planning.
cross_references: NTIA’s Manual of Regulations and Procedures for Federal Radio Frequency Management ("Redbook")
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: If the FS-Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Office determines that an RFA is exempt from disclosure under Freedom of Information Act of 1996, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 552, as amended, the RFA will be accompanied by a justification letter stating the specific exemption(s) from disclosure under FOIA.
cross_references: Freedom of Information Act of 1996, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 552, as amended
conditions: If the FS-Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Office determines that an RFA is exempt from disclosure under Freedom of Information Act of 1996, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 552, as amended

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA IRAC Representative notifies NTIA of this exemption.
All RFAs will reflect the actual installed configuration.
In accordance with the NTIA Redbook, all RFAs must be reviewed and updated every 5 years.
conditions: every 5 years

policy_statements.source_text: The FAS Representative reviews and updates the RFAs and forwards the results to NTIA.
All wireless operations require radio frequency authorizations from NTIA.
Prior arrangements for sharing USDA wireless systems with other non-USDA entities must be coordinated with the USDA FAS Representative.
policy_statements.target: Prior arrangements for sharing USDA wireless systems with other non-USDA entities

policy_statements.source_text: Arrangements permitting cooperative communications of mutual benefit among Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices on each other’s authorized radio frequencies may be made by a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between Federal units or a cooperative agreement (between Federal and non-Federal units) signed by the responsible official having jurisdiction.
policy_statements.target: Arrangements permitting cooperative communications of mutual benefit among Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices on each other’s authorized radio frequencies

policy_statements.source_text: Cooperative agreements require specific statutory authority.
All cooperative agreements must be shared with the FAS Representative.
Copies of the Mission Area, agency, or staff office MOU must be on file with the Mission Area, agency, or staff office and the USDA FAS Representative.
policy_statements.target: Copies of the Mission Area, agency, or staff office MOU

policy_statements.source_text: A formal MOU between units within USDA Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices is not required.
policy_statements.target: formal MOU between units within USDA Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Arrangements among Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices within USDA, or with external agencies (Federal or non-Federal), must be forwarded to the USDA FAS Representative when authorizations or licenses are required.
policy_statements.target: Arrangements among Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices within USDA, or with external agencies (Federal or non-Federal)
conditions: when authorizations or licenses are required

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must adhere to the regulations governing Citizens Band (CB) Radio Service in the NTIA Redbook when there is a need to communicate between Federal Government and non-Federal Government stations.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: regulations governing Citizens Band (CB) Radio Service in the NTIA Redbook
conditions: when there is a need to communicate between Federal Government and non-Federal Government stations

policy_statements.source_text: CB communications between Federal Government entities are prohibited.
policy_statements.target: CB communications between Federal Government entities

policy_statements.source_text: Acquisition of FRS is prohibited, and no waivers will be granted.

USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office Spectrum Management Liaison Officers may delegate to the radio system operator the authority to program or change frequencies for which the system operator is responsible and has copies of RFAs, MOUs, or Cooperative Agreements.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office Spectrum Management Liaison Officers
conditions: for which the system operator is responsible and has copies of RFAs, MOUs, or Cooperative Agreements

policy_statements.source_text: Individuals who are delegated the authority to reprogram or change frequencies in transmitters must have:
A formal delegation that includes the specific frequencies that they are authorized to program or change; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Individuals who are delegated the authority to reprogram or change frequencies in transmitters

policy_statements.source_text: Knowledge of the terms and limitations of the RFA or license for each specific frequency being changed or programmed.
policy_statements.actor_name: Individuals who are delegated the authority to reprogram or change frequencies in transmitters

policy_statements.source_text: USDA radio equipment will not be programmed to operate outside the constraints of the RFA, license, or arrangement.
Interference with frequencies authorized for use by USDA radio systems will be reported to the USDA FAS Representative for resolution if the problem cannot be resolved locally.
policy_statements.target: Interference with frequencies authorized for use by USDA radio systems
conditions: if the problem cannot be resolved locally

policy_statements.source_text: The NTIA will release information concerning frequency assignments to the requester unless the FS-FOIA Office designates the assignment as FOIA-exempt.
conditions: unless the FS-FOIA Office designates the assignment as FOIA-exempt

policy_statements.source_text: Most USDA frequency assignments are not exempt from release under FOIA.
The NTIA Redbook mandates that the sharing of Government-owned radio resources with other Federal Agencies is required when deemed to be cost-effective and savings can be achieved.
policy_statements.target: sharing of Government-owned radio resources with other Federal Agencies
conditions: when deemed to be cost-effective and savings can be achieved

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, or other Federal Agencies may be required to share systems with other USDA Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices in areas where frequencies are not available, or the traffic does not justify separate systems.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, or other Federal Agencies
conditions: in areas where frequencies are not available, or the traffic does not justify separate systems

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will not provide radio communications services to non-Federal entities or to the private sector except as provided in specific laws and regulations.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: except as provided in specific laws and regulations

policy_statements.source_text: Such use will be approved by the USDA IRAC Representative prior to providing such services.
conditions: prior to providing such services

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements for use of non-Federal radio systems, such as microwave (other than common carrier), will be coordinated with the USDA IRAC Representative.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements for use of non-Federal radio systems

policy_statements.source_text: Technical assistance and advice pertaining to system design, equipment selection, sources of supply, and technical specifications may be obtained through the USDA TSC Representative.
policy_statements.target: Technical assistance and advice pertaining to system design, equipment selection, sources of supply, and technical specifications

policy_statements.source_text: All radio equipment will meet NTIA standards unless waived by the USDA IRAC Representative.
conditions: unless waived by the USDA IRAC Representative

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will perform actions to ensure excessed radio transmitting equipment can no longer transmit on the frequencies originally assigned (e.g., erasing the program, removing the frequency determining device) prior to declaring the equipment as excess property or otherwise transferring or disposing of the equipment pursuant to the Agriculture Property Management Regulation.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: prior to declaring the equipment as excess property or otherwise transferring or disposing of the equipment pursuant to the Agriculture Property Management Regulation

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Provide leadership and direction for Departmentwide radio communications initiatives;
Provide advice and assistance to Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices regarding radio telecommunications services and facilities; and
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Apportion and collect the annual NTIA spectrum fees, and prepare and track corresponding paperwork.
The ENS Director will:
Establish procedures for monitoring, measuring, reporting, and enforcing compliance with this DR;
Oversee Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with this policy;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with this policy

policy_statements.source_text: Serve, or delegate a representative to serve, on NTIA’s Policy and Plans Steering Group (PPSG);
policy_statements.target: NTIA’s Policy and Plans Steering Group (PPSG)

policy_statements.source_text: Review and render decisions on Mission Area, agency, and staff office telecommunications policy waiver requests; and
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office telecommunications policy waiver requests

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an electronic file of approved waivers.
The FS Chief will:
Represent USDA on the IRAC, SPS, and the FAS of the NTIA;
policy_statements.target: IRAC, SPS, and the FAS of the NTIA

policy_statements.source_text: Establish and ensure compliance with policies, standards, and procedures for allotting and assigning frequencies within USDA;
policy_statements.target: policies, standards, and procedures for allotting and assigning frequencies within USDA

policy_statements.source_text: License and assign radio frequencies for use by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices, and maintain the records related to these actions; and
Inspect USDA’s radio operations to ensure compliance with national and international regulations and policies for radio frequency use.
Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors will:

Designate a Spectrum Management Liaison Officer to represent the Mission Area, agency, or staff office in all matters pertaining to radio communications and frequency management if the Mission Area, agency, or staff office uses transmitting devices requiring frequency assignments;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office
conditions: if the Mission Area, agency, or staff office uses transmitting devices requiring frequency assignments

policy_statements.source_text: Notify the IRAC Representative when there is a change in Spectrum Management Liaison Officers;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
conditions: when there is a change in Spectrum Management Liaison Officers

policy_statements.source_text: Include the radio program in the budget planning process as identified in Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Circular A-11, Preparation, Submission, and Execution of the Budget; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Circular A-11, Preparation, Submission, and Execution of the Budget

policy_statements.source_text: Prepare and maintain a strategic plan when the radio program within a Mission Area, agency, or staff office expands and becomes a significant capital asset (significant procurement, operating, or maintenance cost).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
conditions: when the radio program within a Mission Area, agency, or staff office expands and becomes a significant capital asset (significant procurement, operating, or maintenance cost)

policy_statements.source_text: This plan will be provided to the ENS Director and the USDA IRAC Representative upon origination and at each update.
conditions: upon origination and at each update

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA IRAC Representative will:
Ensure compliance with this policy, consistent with the delegations to the FS Chief in 7 CFR § 2.60(a)(27).
conditions: consistent with the delegations to the FS Chief in 7 CFR § 2.60(a)(27)

policy_statements.source_text: Engineer, select, and acquire frequencies to support validated requirements;
Authorize USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to use specific radio frequencies if their application for a radio frequency meets the spectrum requirements of the NTIA;
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: if their application for a radio frequency meets the spectrum requirements of the NTIA

policy_statements.source_text: Provide interagency coordination and negotiation on frequencies, as required by NTIA;
conditions: as required by NTIA

policy_statements.source_text: Resolve interface problems encountered or created by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices when such problems are caused by assignment incompatibilities and cannot be resolved by the operating unit;
policy_statements.target: interface problems encountered or created by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when such problems are caused by assignment incompatibilities and cannot be resolved by the operating unit

policy_statements.source_text: Review and provide comments on frequency applications submitted by Government and civilian agencies in order to protect USDA frequency assignments;
policy_statements.target: frequency applications submitted by Government and civilian agencies

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as a member on all NTIA committees and subcommittees dealing with frequency management;
policy_statements.target: all NTIA committees and subcommittees dealing with frequency management

policy_statements.source_text: Provide guidance to USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices in the development of frequency plans that support future systems;
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain frequency engineering and control records of USDA frequency resources; and
policy_statements.target: frequency engineering and control records of USDA frequency resources

policy_statements.source_text: Provide training to USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices in basic frequency management.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA FAS Representative will:
Be responsible for frequency assignment actions, support, and interference resolutions for all devices that require assigned frequencies to operate;
policy_statements.target: frequency assignment actions, support, and interference resolutions for all devices that require assigned frequencies to operate

policy_statements.source_text: Process requests for RFAs for all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices; and
policy_statements.target: requests for RFAs for all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Establish procedures to protect against harmful interference that could result in loss of life or property, and coordinate any required resolution.
policy_statements.target: procedures to protect against harmful interference that could result in loss of life or property

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA TSC Representative will:
Provide technical advice on electromagnetic compatibility of new Government systems that operate nationwide and answering questions that USDA has on systems that may affect USDA operations; and
policy_statements.target: electromagnetic compatibility of new Government systems that operate nationwide

policy_statements.source_text: Provide technical assistance and training on spectrum management to USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA SPS Representative will be responsible for assisting in the development of recommendations regarding spectrum support for new systems submitted by Federal Agencies.
policy_statements.target: development of recommendations regarding spectrum support for new systems submitted by Federal Agencies

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Spectrum Management Liaison Officers will:
Serve as principal point of contact (POC) for all matters relating to radio communications and frequency management;

policy_statements.source_text: Review and recommend to the USDA IRAC Representative, on an ongoing basis, revisions to the NTIA Redbook.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Spectrum Management Liaison Officers

Be familiar with NTIA policies; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Spectrum Management Liaison Officers

policy_statements.target: all radio frequencies used by the Mission Area, agency, or staff office

conditions: each year

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to conform to this policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: In the event that a specific policy requirement cannot be met, Mission Area, agency, and staff office system owners may submit a policy waiver request to the ENS Director at ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office system owners
conditions: In the event that a specific policy requirement cannot be met

policy_statements.source_text: The waiver request will explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls/actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating controls/actions provide a similar or greater level of defense or compliance than the policy requirement.

Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors will address all policy waiver request memoranda to the ENS Director, and submit the waiver request to ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov for review and determination.

policy_statements.source_text: Waivers to stipulations of this directive that have been granted approval by the ENS Director and that are associated with a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) control will be recorded and tracked as a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) item in the USDA Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. § 3551, et seq., data management and reporting tool.

policy_statements.target: Waivers to stipulations of this directive
conditions: that have been granted approval by the ENS Director

policy_statements.source_text: Waivers will expire at the end of the fiscal year or 6 months from the date of approval, whichever is longer.
conditions: at the end of the fiscal year or 6 months from the date of approval, whichever is longer

policy_statements.source_text: Unless otherwise specified, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will review and renew approved policy waivers every fiscal year.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: Unless otherwise specified
every fiscal year

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for radio frequency management.
This DR applies to those USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices using radio communications and spectrum management.
